text:
emma_sales: Heads up — Mercuria POC (Private on-prem) hitting intermittent 503s and huge TTFTs. Small prompts ~300ms but long-session requests (2k+ tokens) spike to ~10s. Client demo Friday. Need triage.

raj_se: noted — are they on a single-node pool? Do we have pool metrics? Any difference between warmup and steady-state?

olga_infra: single-node cluster behind their LB. Memory constrained (32GB GPU mem). Observed frequent KV cache evictions due to many distinct session prefixes. That would cause cold KV rebuilds and long first-token times. Also saw a flurry of 503s from the runtime when the batcher queue got overloaded.

vince_oncall: pulled sampled logs from node mercuria-a: 
```
[2024-08-12T09:02:11Z] req=mx1 code=200 latency_ms=320 cache_hit=true
[2024-08-12T09:02:22Z] req=mx2 code=503 component=batcher reason=queue_overflow
[2024-08-12T09:02:23Z] req=mx3 code=200 latency_ms=10240 cache_hit=false prefix_len=2048
[2024-08-12T09:02:25Z] req=mx4 code=200 latency_ms=350 cache_hit=true
```
Pattern: bursts -> batcher overflow -> 503s -> requests routed/replayed -> some hit cold cache -> TTFT spike.

raj_se: two-pronged fix: (1) reduce max_batch_window_ms and cap batch size to prevent batcher queue growth, (2) enforce session affinity + persistent prefix cache per-session so long histories don't rebuild on node hop. Also consider trimming old history server-side.

claire_product: we have a "persistent prefix cache" feature for Dedicated; for Private on-prem we expose config knobs. Olga, can you enable per-session cache persistence and set max_prefix_tokens=1024 as a demo?

olga_infra: applying changes now. Also increasing batcher_thread_count and setting batch config: 
```
batcher:
  max_batch_window_ms: 8
  max_batch_tokens: 2048
  max_concurrent_batches: 6
session_cache:
  mode: persistent
  max_prefix_tokens: 1024
  max_sessions_per_node: 120
```
Deploying canary to mercuria-a.

deploy-bot: canary deploy started for mercuria-a (commit: fa7b12)

vince_oncall: after canary (10m sample): 
```
[2024-08-12T09:12:30Z] req=mx10 code=200 latency_ms=340 cache_hit=true
[2024-08-12T09:12:42Z] req=mx11 code=200 latency_ms=410 cache_hit=true
[2024-08-12T09:12:55Z] req=mx12 code=200 latency_ms=860 cache_hit=false prefix_len=1800
```
503s stopped in the sampled window, TTFT spikes reduced but still occasional cold path for very long prefixes.

raj_se: follow-ups: add client-side prefix trimming or delta-history (send incremental turns instead of full 2k each request). Example snippet for clients: 
```
# client pseudo
if len(history_tokens) > 1024:
  history_tokens = history_tokens[-1024:]
send(context=history_tokens + new_prompt)
```
Also we should instrument cache_miss_rate and batcher_queue_length alerts.

emma_sales: security question from Mercuria: EU-only data residency + customer-managed KMS for on-prem. Also they asked about data deletion guarantees for Private.

olga_infra: Private on-prem satisfies residency. For KMS: we support customer-provided key material via local KMS/HSM integrations; we can provide a brief on key rotation and access controls. Data deletion: we have a documented wipe procedure for dedicated nodes and can provide page-level steps and attestations. I'll upload the docs to the deal folder.

dlp-bot: Reminder: Mercuria requested redaction of PII in logs. Enable PII-filtering plugin on the ingestion path if not already on.

claire_product: product note: For long-term scale we recommend either (A) scale node count so session distribution keeps cache warm, or (B) move to Dedicated pools with larger GPU mem and persistent cache across nodes. Pricing impact: Dedicated / Reserved node adds baseline cost but fixes these tail-latency issues. I can sketch numbers.

emma_sales: plan for demo: 1) Olga to confirm canary stable, 2) Raj to provide client trimming sample + alert rules, 3) Olga to upload KMS + deletion docs, 4) Emma to send revised SOW with dedicated option and cost delta. Can we reconvene tomorrow 10am CET?

olga_infra: canary stable from infra side, no 503s in last 15m. Uploading docs now.

raJ_se: (typo) will send runbook in thread.

emma_sales: thanks everyone 64f — I'll schedule the 10am CET sync and include Mercuria stakeholders.
